input.question: Why aren't high rise office fires more common/unsurvivable?
input.ground_truth: They used to, then builders got wise to it. Now we build high rises out of concrete and glass, which don't catch on fire. We restrict how much flammable material is used on the floors of high rises and don't allow anything flammable at all in the stairwells (that's why the stairs are pretty much always barren concrete with metal railings), which makes it more difficult for the fires to spread between floors.

response.prediction: High-rise office fires are not as common or as deadly as people might fear because modern buildings are designed with strict fire safety regulations. These include the use of fire-resistant materials, multiple fire alarms, smoke detectors, and automatic sprinkler systems that can quickly control or extinguish fires. Buildings also have clearly marked and well-practiced evacuation routes, and many have fire doors that help contain flames and smoke to a limited area. Additionally, fire departments are trained to respond to high-rise fires with specialized equipment and personnel. Because of these safety measures, most high-rise office fires are contained quickly and do not become large, uncontrollable disasters.
